title: HTTP, HTTPS and the TLS handshake

videos.script: Lesson 1 fetched a page and read one of its packets. The request was plain text: GET, a path, the name of the site. Anybody on the path could read it, and anybody on the path could have changed it. {{plain}} HTTPS is the same HTTP, inside TLS. TLS is a handshake that agrees on keys, checks who the server is, and then encrypts everything that follows. {{tls}} In this lesson you will speak HTTP by hand, follow a redirect, and read the status codes that point at the website rather than the network. That includes the 502 that means the web server is fine and the program behind it is not. {{http}} Then you will watch a TLS 1.3 handshake, and stand where the internet provider stands, on the office router, to see what HTTPS hides and what it does not. {{observer}} And you will ask curl where the time went: in DNS, in TCP, in TLS, or in the server. {{time}}
